items.author: ys2025-AI
items.summary: Removes two pieces of redundant work on the router-replay hot path: - Router replay only needs the packed rows from; it discards the returned position ids. Add an opt-in so replay packing does not allocate and fill a full position-id tensor.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Removes two pieces of redundant work on the router-replay hot path:

- Router replay only needs the packed rows from `preprocess_thd_engine`; it discards the returned position ids. Add an opt-in `need_position_ids=False` so replay packing does not allocate and fill a full position-id tensor.
- Replay masks are logical masks. Normalize them to `bool` once when they are installed on a `RouterReplay` layer, instead of converting dtype (and moving device) once per layer on every forward.

No semantic change to replay selection: replayed rows still use the captured routes

The encoder-only prefix cache (`--enable-prefix-mm-cache`) keyed a **whole request** and was only consulted when `len(items_per_req) == 1`. In an encoder-disaggregated VLM deployment:

- a fused multi-request encoder batch cannot use the cache at all;
- the cache stores one combined embedding per request instead of the reusable item.

This is the common case for agent screenshots, OCR pages and long image/video prompts.

## Fix

Store and look up encoder embeddings **per media item**:

- full hit: concate

## [Core] Divergence-point prefix-cache salting: `cache_salt_start_idx`

### Motivation

`cache_salt` today is all-or-nothing. A salted request isolates its **entire**
block-hash chain, so two tenants on the same deployment never share a single
cached block — even when their prompts begin with the same thousands of tokens
(shared system prompts, RAG preambles, agent scaffolds). That is the
all-or-nothing tradeoff documented in "Governing the KV Cache: Preventing
Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference"
([arXiv:2608.09225](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09225)), which proposes sal

items.body:
Fix streaming vs non-streaming content divergence in Hermes2ProToolParser.

## Problem
`Hermes2ProToolParser.extract_tool_calls` (non-streaming) kept only the text
preceding the first tool-call tag and silently dropped any trailing content
after the last tool call. The streaming path preserved trailing text, so the
two modes diverged and legitimate output after a tool call was lost.

## Fix
- Non-streaming: keep every part of the response outside tool-call tags as
  content (leading, between consecutive calls, and trailing).
- Streaming: emit trailing content after the last complete tool call

items.title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Bound cache-aware admission probe by request reuse limit
items.author: htang7415
items.summary: Fixes KV cache admission probe using wrong token count by ignoring per-request prefix-cache reuse limits, causing incorrect waiting-queue ranking.
items.body:
## Overview

With `cache_aware_admission_window > 0`, the waiting-queue ranking probe
`KVCacheManager.get_num_cached_tokens` (added in #54625) estimates the hit with
`request.num_tokens - 1`. It ignores the request's prefix-cache reuse limit from
#60960. A prompt-scoring request with `prompt_logprob_start` is therefore ranked
by a resident prefix it is not allowed to adopt. It is admitted ahead of a peer
whose prefix it can actually reuse, and its fresh blocks evict that peer's
cached prefix. The probe now uses `request.get_max_cache_hit_length()`, the
same bound that actual adoption uses.

items.body:
## Motivation

On SM12x (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and the rest of the SM120/SM121 family), the DSA lightning indexer runs as two steps:

1. DeepGEMM's FP8 MQA logits write a `[rows, keys]` fp32 logits tensor.
2. A separate top-k transform reads those logits back to pick 2048 keys per row.

At long context the second step reads every logit again. FlashInfer now ships a fused SM120 indexer, `flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk(..., backend="sm120")` (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7085). It scores the keys and selects the exact top-k in one pass, without writing the logits:

items.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Bump fastokens to 0.3.6
items.author: waynehacking8
items.summary: Bumps fastokens from 0.3.5 to 0.3.6 to fix tokenizer crashes on text containing carriage returns for Hy3 and similar models.
items.body:
## Overview

With `tencent/Hy3` or `tencent/Hy3-preview`, fastokens 0.3.5 fails on any text with a carriage return ("byte 0x0d has no token in vocabulary"), where Hugging Face tokenizers drops the byte. fastokens 0.3.6 (crusoecloud/fastokens#89, fixing crusoecloud/fastokens#88) drops it too and gives the same ids (both models fail in crusoecloud/fastokens#88 and match in the checks on crusoecloud/fastokens#89).

vLLM uses fastokens in two places: the Rust frontend's tokenizer, and the optional Python backend behind `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1`. This PR moves both to 0.3.6.

items.body:
## Problem

With the default overlap scheduler and `--enable-return-routed-experts`, DSpark rollouts return all-zero or stale routed-expert IDs for generated tokens. Target verification computes them, but `TargetVerifyResult` and the final `GenerationBatchResult` drop the deferred capture outputs, so the scheduler never copies them to the host. With routing replay in RL (Miles R3), the trainer replays these IDs, so generated tokens are trained through expert 0 instead of the experts the rollout actually used.

items.title: [Fix] hicache: reject short Mooncake zero-copy reads
items.author: YaoleWu
items.summary: SGLang's hit path only checks, so a destination larger than the stored object is accepted as a hit even though only part of it was written. The rest of the page keeps stale bytes.
items.body:
## Problem

Mooncake's zero-copy `batch_get_into*` returns the **stored object's byte count** as a positive result. SGLang's hit path only checks `result > 0`, so a destination larger than the stored object is accepted as a hit even though only part of it was written. The rest of the page keeps stale bytes.

The same boundary also trusts the result vector length. A short result vector can be sliced into misaligned per-pool results, and the put path accepts zero/negative pointers and sizes before calling native.

This matters for HiCache deployments where keys are shared across reconfigurations

items.author: beinan
items.summary: Selective prefill can issue queries at positions while retaining a 17-token KV sequence. Treating those queries as the contiguous tail gives the earlier queries the wrong causal visibility.
items.body:
## Motivation

Selective prefill can issue queries at positions `[0, 7, 16]` while retaining a 17-token KV sequence. Treating those queries as the contiguous tail `[14, 15, 16]` gives the earlier queries the wrong causal visibility. items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: At the time, level-2 sleep discarded the whole pool. The fusion's collective kernel keeps its state in that pool: the Lamport flags and the peer pointer table. [Discussion: ✅ Triggered for commit.]
items.body:
## Purpose

#64583 turned off the Kimi-K3 latent-MoE tail fusion whenever sleep mode is on, and logged a warning. At the time, level-2 sleep discarded the whole `weights` pool. The fusion's collective kernel keeps its state in that pool: the Lamport flags (`_routed_flags`, `_shared_flags`) and the peer pointer table. None of these are parameters, so they were lost on wake.

Since #66010, level 2 discards only allocations that hold nothing but parameters, and offloads and restores everything else at the same address. That state now survives sleep, so this PR removes the fallback and its warning

items.author: yifjiang
items.summary: Mooncake PD cancellation can retire original request KV/cache locks, metadata or device destination slots before outstanding native writes are known to have drained. The legacy synchronous transfer error path can leave completion unknown, while the device dest…
items.body:
Mooncake PD cancellation can retire original request KV/cache locks, metadata or device destination slots before outstanding native writes are known to have drained. The legacy synchronous transfer error path can leave completion unknown, while the device destination deadline permits release without a drain ACK.

Retain native source ownership through queued chunks and worker bookkeeping, then release through attention TP/CP roster and completion consensus. Require the existing generation-bound drain ACK for Mooncake device destinations. Mooncake startup rejects disabling this drain protocol.

items.title: [Bugfix][Offload] Re-offload UVA params whose data replace_parameter rebound
items.author: suryakiranc
items.summary: Fixes UVA parameter offloading regression where replace_parameter-rebound tensors silently stayed on device instead of being re-offloaded, causing CUDA OOM.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #66264.

`replace_parameter` keeps the existing `Parameter` object (and its `_vllm_is_uva_offloaded` marker) and rebinds `.data` to the new device tensor when a repacked weight does not fit the old storage. `device_loading_context` only re-offloaded when the marker was missing, so these weights silently stayed resident on the device after `process_weights_after_loading`.

This change records each UVA-offloaded parameter's `data_ptr()` on entry and re-offloads if the marker is missing **or** the pointer changed. In-place copies (same pointer) are unaffected.

Related: #58178,

items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: HiCache writes a prefix to L3 storage once, when it is first backed up to host. If the storage backend later loses those objects (for example, a storage node restarts), the prefix is never written again while it keeps hitting in L1/L2, so the holes in L3 only …
items.body:
## Motivation

HiCache writes a prefix to L3 storage once, when it is first backed up to host. If the storage backend later loses those objects (for example, a storage node restarts), the prefix is never written again while it keeps hitting in L1/L2, so the holes in L3 only close when some request misses and recomputes the prefix. items.author: mynotwo
items.summary: Changing LM-head output precision can change a greedy token even with identical hidden states: BF16 output rounding can turn distinct scores into an exact tie. The sampling reference currently does not explain how CUDA resolves that tie or how this relates to …
items.body:
## Motivation

Changing LM-head output precision can change a greedy token even with identical hidden states: BF16 output rounding can turn distinct scores into an exact tie. The sampling reference currently does not explain how CUDA resolves that tie or how this relates to the FP32 LM-head option.

## Modifications

- Document lowest-token-ID tie-breaking on the CUDA argmax path and clarify that `sampling_seed` does not resolve greedy ties.
- Explain FP32-output GEMM on the standard unquantized CUDA path, including unchanged operand/storage dtypes and the limits of comparisons across precisio

items.title: [Perf][Attention] Tune single-request FP16 Triton decode on SM80
items.author: KuanJia
items.summary: The default FP16 Triton decode path scans KV in 16-token tiles. For single-request long-context decoding, this incurs many loop iterations, address calculations and online-softmax updates.
items.body:
## Overview

The default FP16 Triton decode path scans KV in 16-token tiles. For single-request long-context decoding, this incurs many loop iterations, address calculations and online-softmax updates. This PR widens the KV tile to 64 and tunes the launch configuration on SM80 to reduce that overhead, reusing the existing attention kernel and reduction.

## Claims

- **25.1%–59.3% higher Qwen3-8B decode throughput** on a single A100 with TRITON_ATTN.
- **2.06–2.19x faster attention operations** at 256K–2M with the model's Q/KV/head shape.

## Validation

A100-SXM4-40GB, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132,

items.title: [Fix] attention: Account for allocator cache in MQA logits budgets
items.author: YingHREN
items.summary: The shared MQA logits budget uses driver-visible free memory but does not count unused blocks held by PyTorch's caching allocator. A warmed server can report zero driver-free bytes while the allocator still has several GiB not occupied by tensors.
items.body:
## Motivation

The shared MQA logits budget uses driver-visible free memory but does not count unused blocks held by PyTorch's caching allocator. A warmed server can report zero driver-free bytes while the allocator still has several GiB not occupied by tensors. The current helper then returns a one-byte budget, and the row planner falls back to one row per chunk.

For a 7,392 x 16,384 fp32 logits matrix (462 MiB), this can mean 7,392 chunks instead of one. The paged DSV4 path still launches logits and top-k for each chunk in each layer, even though current upstream reuses the chunk metada

items.body:
## Purpose

Lookahead block hashes are now used by core prefix caching and by every KV connector. With them, an EAGLE, EAGLE3 or MTP prefix hit already proves that the draft KV at the block boundary is reusable. The legacy approach drops the last matched block and compensates for it everywhere else. It is no longer needed, so this PR removes the drop and makes lookahead hashes the only behavior.

This PR is stacked on #65448, which can enable all connectors lookahead hashes.

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Relay multimodal requests to later PP stages without raw features
items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: Strips raw multimodal feature tensors before relaying requests through non-first pipeline parallel stages, avoiding costly pickle/send of image data that downstream ranks never consume.
items.body:
## Motivation

Under pipeline parallelism, the first PP stage relays every newly received request to the next stage (`_pp_send_pyobj_to_next_stage(recv_reqs)` → `point_to_point_pyobj`, i.e. pickle + gloo send). Every later stage then rebroadcasts the object to its attention TP/CP peers and relays it again.

With `mm_feature_transport=cpu`, `RequestReceiver._finalize_shm_features` has already materialized each image's raw feature tensor into the request object by that point. For example, a 1080p image is about 6 MB of CHW uint8. All of it gets serialized at every hop on the scheduler threads.

items.summary: Speed up the CPU side quadric error metric (QEM) mesh decimation used by Hunyuan3D Paint preprocessing, without changing the intended decimation behavior. This PR contains three focused optimizations: - P5-C: Packed face deduplication: Replace row wise on sort…
items.body:
Follow up for #48075

## Summary

Speed up the CPU side quadric error metric (QEM) mesh decimation used by Hunyuan3D Paint preprocessing, without changing the intended decimation behavior.

This PR contains three focused optimizations:

- **P5-C: Packed face deduplication:** Replace row wise `np.unique(..., axis=0)` on sorted triangle indices with packed `int64` face keys. Cast before multiplication and retain the original NumPy path when the key range could overflow `int64`.
- **P5-E: Undirected edge keys:** Use elementwise `min`/`max` to form edge keys instead of sorting each edge p

items.title: Fix dataloader checkpoint directory creation on every writing rank
items.author: jwills
items.summary: When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts.
items.body:
When external dataloader state is saved per data-parallel rank, only DP rank 0 currently creates the checkpoint's parent directory. A distributed barrier synchronizes ranks but does not guarantee directory visibility across node-local filesystem mounts. A nonzero writing rank can therefore reach `torch.save` without its parent directory and fail.

Call `ensure_directory_exists` on every rank that writes a state file. Rank-independent loaders retain their rank-0-only writes. Extend the explicit-process-groups regression test, which uses DP rank 3, to assert that the parent directory exists.

items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Fixes three scheduler bugs: leaked memory from aborted PD prefill requests, stuck streaming sessions on rejection, and PP loop ignoring pause_generation during inference.
items.body: - **PD prefill: clear the bootstrap room of an aborted request.** A prefill request aborted after it left the bootstrap queue is retired through `release_prefill_sender(abort_sender=True)`, which only called `sender.abort()`. ## Overview

`_w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm` forms its A-row and C-row offsets (`offs_am * stride_am`, `offs_cm * stride_cm`) in int32, so once `M * K` or `M * N` passes 2**31, rows past that bound read A from, and write C to, the wrong address. ## Overview

This PR fixes an issue in the fast detokenizer where adjacent non-special added tokens can show up as raw token content instead of decoded whitespace.

## Motivation

> **Workaround.** This hard-codes two shapes until flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9020 lands. items.title: [Perf][Core] Look up single-group prefix-cache hits with one dict get per block
items.author: davidteather
items.summary: calls once per prompt block until the first miss. For single-group (dense) models that is five Python calls and two allocations per block, on the scheduler thread, on every admission, scaling with the cached prompt length.
items.body:
## Overview

`FullAttentionManager.find_longest_cache_hit` calls `BlockPool.get_cached_block` once per prompt block
until the first miss. For single-group (dense) models that is five Python calls and two allocations per
block, on the scheduler thread, on every admission, scaling with the cached prompt length. This adds
`BlockHashToBlockMap.get_prefix_blocks` (one dict get per block with the group suffix hoisted) and uses
it when there is one KV cache group; multi-group managers keep the existing loop.
`_get_num_evictable_blocks` becomes a list comprehension. Scheduling decisions are unchanged.

items.author: hongxiayang
items.summary: At DCP1, the AMD Kimi-K3 specialized decode refuses to start whenever M1 cannot serve the MLA layers. Kimi-K3.1 (#65685) never qualifies: its DSA layers keep an KV cache, which M1 does not read.
items.body:
## Overview

At DCP1, the AMD Kimi-K3 specialized decode (`decode_backend=latency_specialized`) refuses to start whenever M1
cannot serve the MLA layers. Kimi-K3.1 (#65685) never qualifies: its DSA layers keep an `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache,
which M1 does not read. On ROCm at DCP1, K3.1 therefore gets vLLM's decode only. This PR serves DCP1 without M1
the way DCP8 already does: the MLA layers run vLLM's attention ops, then K2.

## Claims

- **Kimi-K3.1 Pro, ROCm, TP8 DCP1:** the specialized decode now runs. Decode step time is 38% lower at

items.title: [Feature][Hybrid] K0 spec-window slot release for hybrid mamba models
items.author: michael-gpu
items.summary: Releases idle speculative-window slots at K=0 crossings for hybrid Mamba+attention models in MTP spec-decoding, admitting waiting requests and reclaiming slots on promotion.
items.body:
# [Feature][Hybrid] K0 spec-window slot release for hybrid mamba models

## Overview

Hybrid-state (mamba + full-attention) models running MTP speculative decoding keep every request's speculative window allocated even when the dynamic spec-tier table (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`) resolves the step to K=0 at high batch counts — at a c32 crossing that is most of the pinned KV. This PR releases running rows' idle windows back to the pool at the K=0 crossing, admits waiting rows at the K=0 tier while the pool is pressured (the window born as null row slots), and promotes released rows

items.title: [CPU] Support 2D (batched) weights in rms_norm, fixing DFlash acceptance on CPU
items.author: jimburtoft
items.summary: Fixes CPU rms_norm kernel to correctly index 2D batched weights by row, aligning with CUDA behavior and restoring DFlash speculative decoding acceptance on CPU.
items.body:
## Overview

The CPU `rms_norm` kernel ignores the row dimension of a 2D (batched) weight and applies row 0 to every token. The CUDA kernel selects the weight row by the outermost input index (#46761). DFlash relies on that for its fused per-layer context-key norm (`DFlashQwen3Model._normalize_context_k`), so on CPU every draft layer after the first gets wrongly normalized context keys. This PR adds the same 2D-weight semantics and shape checks to the CPU kernel and enables the existing batched-weight test on CPU.

## Claims

- CPU `rms_norm` with a `[input.size(0), hidden]` weight now match

## Motivation

With `SGLANG_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND` unset, `init_threads_binding` pins one OpenMP thread per physical core of the rank's NUMA node. A container started with `--cpus=N` (or a Kubernetes `limits.cpu`) keeps the full cpuset, so the rank runs more busy threads than its CFS quota and is throttled in every scheduling period.

This is the SGLang counterpart of my vLLM change vllm-project/vllm#61833, which caps vLLM's CPU worker the same way.

In the default (unset) path of `init_threads_binding`, cap each rank's CPU list by its share of the cgroup CPU quota:

## Overview

On gfx1151, bf16 W4A16 layers fall off a cliff at decode-sized M.

## Overview

## Description

Muse Spark's DFlash drafter on VANILLA attention keeps its context K/V in a private arena outside the KV cache manager. items.title: Apply the expert gradient scale under average_in_collective
items.author: Connor-XY
items.summary: Makes Megatron-FSDP v1 apply the expert gradient scale when is set. With, picked the AVG reduction and dropped the scaling factor. [Discussion: Auto-sync is disabled for draft pull requests in this repository.]
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

## Description

This PR adds an opt-in cap on the split-KV count of the DSpark MLA drafter's CuTe DSL attention. Set it with `TLLM_DSPARK_MLA_MAX_SPLIT_KV`.

items.author: yijingl-nvidia
items.summary: This PR makes the Kimi K3 KDA fused prefill convolution faster on batches with mixed sequence lengths. It also fixes a warmup failure when the conv-state pool is large.
items.body:
## Description

This PR makes the Kimi K3 KDA fused prefill convolution faster on batches with mixed sequence lengths. It also fixes a warmup failure when the conv-state pool is large.

Before this PR, the convolution launched one CTA per run of the longest sequence, for every sequence. On a batch with one long and many short sequences, most CTAs exit at once. At 96 heads, the convolution reached only 36-64% of the HBM limit on real mixes of 16K-32K-token contexts. Also, it rejected any state pool with 2^31 or more elements in total. KV cache manager V2 keeps the states of all layers of a slot

items.title: [Proposal] Configurable hidden-state feedback for HybridModel
items.author: kwangjunahn
items.summary: Adds a configurable hidden-state feedback framework to Megatron for integrating previous-token hidden states into current inputs, supporting additive and gated fusion variants.
items.body:
## Problem and motivation

Add support for feeding the previous token’s final hidden state into the current token’s input, following the shared idea in [Full-bandwidth Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08888v2) and [Recycler](https://seed.bytedance.com/en/public_papers/recycler-cost-free-latent-reasoning-via-hidden-state-recycling).

Both methods introduce a continuous connection across token positions while retaining one backbone evaluation per decoded token, plus a small fusion operation. They differ in how they combine hidden states with embeddings and how they train that connection.

## Description

When one streamed chunk ends a MiniMax-M3 tool call and starts the next, `parse_streaming_increment` sent the whole buffer to `detect_and_parse`. That returns the text after the last closer as content, so the half-received second call went out as text, and the rest of it arrived with no opener and went out as text too. The call was lost.

items.body:
## Description

Related to #21470. An oversized context can pass request admission and reach the V2 cache manager with a page-index table bounded by the physical pool. Enlarging that table alone changes the immediate sizing exception into repeated allocation failure, while increasing page-table memory, copy work, and exposure to existing 32-bit indexing limits.

Keep page-index staging bounded by the manager's allocatable sequence length and generation headroom. Supply the existing executor admission budget for ordinary dense, full-attention V2 target managers in aggregated serving with CP=1.

## What does this PR do?

An abort forces an active request to finish on its next step: the handler
sets the request's output length to its KV offset plus its query length, so

toward the length only if they are accepted, so the request finishes on the
next step only when every draft is accepted. Otherwise it keeps its row, its
KV blocks and its share of the step budget for up to

than the step's token buffers, and the forward fails in

## Description

Triton specializes integer arguments on `== 1` and `% 16 == 0` and pointer arguments on 16-byte alignment, and compiles a new kernel variant whenever one of those keys changes. Several speculative-decoding step kernels take arguments whose keys follow the batch composition, so they compile new variants mid-serving, after warmup:

- request counts
- first-row offsets
- pair-layout offsets derived from the row count
- views sliced at the number of context requests

items.title: [MFSDP] Bypass gradient packing when inner reduction is unnecessary
items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: When gradients can reach their accumulation placements without inner communication, MFSDP still allocates a packing buffer and copies gradients through it. Accumulate directly into instead, including HSDP/HFSDP with a singleton inner DP axis.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

When gradients can reach their accumulation placements without inner communication, MFSDP still allocates a packing buffer and copies gradients through it. Accumulate directly into `main_grad` instead, including HSDP/HFSDP with a singleton inner DP axis.

Each parameter group computes `requires_inner_reduction` from its existing mesh and gradient placements. Groups requiring communication retain the packed path. Other groups accumulate on compute in `main_grad.dtype`, avoiding communication-dtype

items.title: Add an optional copy-engine gather/scatter for FsdpMuon
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Muon's optimizer step gathers each weight matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back. Those transfers are NCCL send/recv, which run on the GPU's SMs.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Muon's optimizer step gathers each weight matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back. Those transfers are NCCL send/recv, which run on the GPU's SMs. This PR adds an optional path that moves them with peer-to-peer copies on the GPU's copy engines instead, so the transfers use no SMs. Enable it with `FSDP_MUON_CE=1`. items.title: Add an optional TensorAtomic placement for MCore MFSDP v2 dense parameters
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back. This PR adds an optional alternative: with `MFSDP_TENSOR_ATOMIC=1`, every dense parameter stays whole on one owner rank (the `TensorAtomic` placement), so the Muon step needs no gather or scatter. Owners are chosen greedily to balance the Newton-Schulz cost. The plan depends only on parameter shapes, so every rank computes the same one. Experts keep their own mesh.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

items.author: JonnesLin
items.summary: built its train/val s without a, so every iterator construction drew a from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted ru…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

items.body:
## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

How it happens:

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.summary: Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups.

Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups. Preserve the first failure and raise it in the consumer with its original cause; stop scheduling work, cancel in-flight tasks, and prevent automatic replacement of the failed worker. Explicit ABORTED retries and intentional shutdown cancellation keep their existing behavior.

Closes https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/2399

At `5bae5bb7928d65906e24e99f5b5d3f99a4daaf93`, per-sample training metadata is lost at two points in `RolloutManager`:

items.title: fix: restore actor weights before initial rollout sync
items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

items.author: LOGO127
items.summary: Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path. Under CUDA autocast, can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

## Description

items.author: MrCapricornLiu
items.summary: PPO currently adds the scalar reward to CP rank 0. With zigzag context-parallel slicing, padding can put the final response prediction on another rank.
items.body:
PPO currently adds the scalar reward to CP rank 0. With zigzag context-parallel slicing, padding can put the final response prediction on another rank. For example, total length 9 and response length 3 at CP=2 leave rank 0 with no response predictions, so indexing its last reward raises IndexError. If rank 0 owns earlier response predictions, the reward is instead attached to the wrong time step.

Use the existing CP token offsets to find the shard containing the final response token. CP=1 retains the existing behavior, and the per-token KL reward remains unchanged.

items.title: fix(rollout): measure each engine's host instead of deriving it from its rank
items.author: kaysonyu
items.summary: Previously, derived each engine's node from its rank via and then stamped every engine in a 'virtual node' with the first engine's measured IP. This formula is only valid when every server group starts at a physical-node boundary.
items.body:

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. items.body:
## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

items.body:
## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.
